title: Pico + NeoPixel prototype tray
brief: An open, dimensioned tray and a provisional 5 V electrical prototype for a Raspberry Pi Pico Rev3 and Adafruit NeoPixel Stick #1426.
summary: Two-board tray checked against manufacturer STEP models. Proposed 5 V data and power path is source-backed but unbuilt; supply, harness, auxiliary-part fit and measurements remain open.

parts.name: Raspberry Pi Pico Rev3
parts.detail: Official STEP envelope including micro-USB overhang: 52.3 × 21.0 × 3.73 mm. Board specification says 51 × 21 × 1 mm PCB. Four 2.1 mm mounting holes. No physical board was measured.
parts.voltage: USB 5 V input; board logic 3.3 V

parts.name: Adafruit NeoPixel Stick #1426, 8 RGB pixels
parts.detail: Manufacturer product page gives 51.1 × 10.22 × 3.19 mm; manufacturer STEP measures 50.8 × 10.16 × 2.6 mm. Tray check uses published X/Y and rounded-up 3.2 mm Z. Eight RGB pixels can draw up to 480 mA total at full white by Adafruit's 60 mA/pixel estimate. Exact shipped LED revision and real draw need checking.
parts.voltage: 5 V nominal; confirm exact product revision

parts.name: Original two-board prototype tray
parts.detail: Editable OpenCascade source and STEP are in examples/pico-neopixel-tray. Open tray with six locator pins and a USB-side notch. Not released for fabrication until cable, fastening, tolerance and print-process checks pass.

parts.name: TI SN74AHCT125N, PDIP-14
parts.detail: Use gate 1: 1OE pin 1 held low, Pico GP2 to 1A pin 2, 1Y pin 3 to series resistor. VCC pin 14, GND pin 7. Tie unused inputs to a defined rail; unused outputs may float. Exact board or breadboard mounting is not in the tray CAD.

parts.name: 470 Ω series data resistor
parts.detail: Place close to Stick DIN, between 74AHCT125 gate-1 output and DIN. Choose a real resistor and verify its value. Not located in tray CAD.

parts.name: 1000 µF polarized capacitor, at least 6.3 V
parts.detail: Across Stick +5 V and GND close to input; check polarity and chosen part dimensions. Not located in tray CAD.

parts.name: 0.1 µF ceramic bypass capacitor
parts.detail: Across SN74AHCT125N VCC pin 14 and GND pin 7, close to the IC per TI. Not located in tray CAD.

parts.name: Regulated 5 V source and distribution harness, exact parts TBD
parts.detail: Provide separate 5 V branches to Pico micro-USB, Stick +5V/GND and level shifter VCC/GND, with common ground. Do not assume the Pico VBUS header or an arbitrary USB host can carry the LED load. Select a source, cable, connector and branching method only after rating checks.

wires.note: Exact supply, cable and branch hardware TBD; no LED power routed through Pico VBUS header.
Use input end. Select a distribution harness rated for worst-case load.
Gate 1OE pin 1 held low. Other OE and A inputs require defined levels; see TI datasheet.
Never connect a 5 V signal to Pico GPIO. Confirm exact Pico header pinout before wiring.
Series resistor is near Stick DIN.
DOUT is left unconnected for one Stick.
Observe polarized capacitor polarity; positive to 5 V.
Place 0.1 µF bypass capacitor close to IC supply pins.

powerRails.name: Proposed shared 5 V rail; source and auxiliary currents open

steps.title: Confirm source model revisions
steps.detail: Download the Raspberry Pi and Adafruit STEP files named in the example README and compare their hashes with the fit report.

steps.title: Check mechanical dimensions
steps.detail: Run the verification script, then measure the exact boards and connector on physical samples before committing to a print.

steps.title: Select and rate the 5 V source
steps.detail: Choose an exact regulated source, dual-branch harness, cable and connectors. The LED upper-bound estimate is 8 × 60 = 480 mA; add measured or sourced Pico and shifter peak currents, then check all ratings with headroom.

steps.title: Assemble the off-tray data interface
steps.detail: With power disconnected, wire Pico GP2 to SN74AHCT125N 1A, hold 1OE low, connect 1Y through 470 Ω to Stick DIN, tie unused IC inputs and add 0.1 µF bypass close to VCC/GND. Verify pin numbering for the purchased package.

steps.title: Connect power and common ground
steps.detail: With power disconnected, branch the same verified 5 V source to Pico micro-USB, Stick +5V/GND and shifter VCC/GND; add 1000 µF capacitor across Stick input with correct polarity. Do not use Pico VBUS as the LED feed in this plan.

steps.title: Bench test before tray assembly
steps.detail: Current-limit the source for initial bring-up, begin at low brightness, then measure worst-case current, rail sag and signal levels with the actual parts. Stop if the supply, cable or connector limits are exceeded.

steps.title: Print a fit coupon
steps.detail: Use the intended material and printer to test locator-pin diameter, wall thickness and board-hole engagement before printing the full tray.

steps.title: Dry-fit unpowered parts
steps.detail: Check board insertion and removal, USB plug access, cable bend, wire clearance and retention without connecting power.

steps.title: Package the auxiliary electronics
steps.detail: Measure the level shifter, capacitors, resistor, harness and USB plug; locate them mechanically, add insulation and strain relief, then revise CAD. They are absent from the current two-board tray model.

notes: Mechanical STEP fit is only for Pico and Stick, with 1.5 mm minimum Pico wall clearance and 3.78 mm published Stick wall clearance. Auxiliary electronics, distribution harness and mating USB plug are not modeled. The 480 mA LED figure is Adafruit’s maximum-white estimate for eight pixels, not a measured assembly draw. Supply rating, Pico peak draw and level-shifter dynamic draw remain unknown, so the power worksheet must stay incomplete. All prices are unknown; no bench wiring or physical fit was performed.
